text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Estonian population was 1.46 million on January 1, 12,200 less than in 1995, statistics officials said.
- Workers of the bankrupt Oru peat plant who have not been paid for three to seven months plan a hunger strike to draw attention to their situation.
- Film makers suspect the Culture Capital Fund of favoring certain studios when allocating money for projects.
- Saving in administration expenses is not only a matter of economy but also of ethics, Economy Minister Jaak Leimannn said.
- County heads are against the project to cut down administration which would cut the number of counties to four.
- The opposition Reform Party presented to parliament a draft law, planning to join the economy, agriculture and transport ministry.
- Hospitals in Tallinn treated at the weekend 100 people who had fallen in the slippery streets, doctors said.
- The government will discuss today the appointment of new ambassadors to Finland, United States and the European Union.
- Appartments in central Tallinn were privatised by city officials who had inside information, the inspection department of the new city council said.
- Prices in 1996 were 23.1 percent higher compared with 1995, statistics officials said.

- The newspaper says that Hansapank, Savings Bank, Tallinna Pank and Foreks Pank are joint owners of a company Prosperitas through which they deal with their own shares and may be able to influence share prices.
